newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica exchange to be computerized in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica exchange to be computerized in 1997.

text.p: The Jamaica Stock Exchange said it plans to be fully computerized by the third quarter of 1997, allowing the exchange to be open for trading five days a week.

This will also allow computerized trading links with the exchanges of the Bahamas, Barbados, the Dominican Republic and Trinidad, according to stock exchange general manager Wain Iton said on Friday. Currently the Jamaica Stock Exchange is open for trading four days each week.

The Kingston-based exchange will also create a computerized depository to be run as a separate company owned by the exchange, brokers and financial institutions, Iton said. The depository's electronic records will replace all existing and future share certificates.

In the United States, the NASDAQ is using US$2.2 million in funding from the Inter-American Development Bank to modernize all five of the Caribbean stock exchanges that will be linked by the new system.
